name: EaseDB
tagline: HKUST research prototype of an in-memory query processor built entirely from cache-oblivious algorithms.
description: EaseDB was a research prototype from Bingsheng He, Yinan Li, Qiong Luo (HKUST) and Dongqing Yang (Peking University), demonstrated at SIGMOD 2007. It explored whether an in-memory relational query processor could be fast on any memory hierarchy without knowing cache sizes or line lengths: data structures, joins, sorting and selection used cache-oblivious algorithms based on recursive partitioning instead of hand-tuned, cache-conscious parameters. The group's companion papers (cache-oblivious nested-loop joins at CIKM 2006, 'Cache-oblivious databases' in TODS 2008) found these designs close to tuned cache-conscious code while being far easier to port. It was never released as a product; it matters as a reference point for hardware-oblivious query processing. (Not to be confused with an unrelated 2013 Ruby file store of the same name on GitHub.)
statusNote: Research prototype (SIGMOD 2007 demo, HKUST); no public release. Ideas live on in cache-aware/oblivious work in in-memory engines.
developer: HKUST and Peking University (B. He, Y. Li, Q. Luo, D. Yang)

pricing.notes: Never distributed; the papers are the only artefact.

strengths: Showed a whole query processor can run without cache-size tuning parameters
Cache-oblivious joins and indexes stayed competitive with tuned cache-conscious code in published experiments
Clear, citable reference for hardware-oblivious database design
weaknesses: Single-threaded, read-only analytical scope; no transactions or persistence
useCases: Studying cache-oblivious algorithms applied to joins, sorting and indexing
Background reading for in-memory analytical engine design
notIdealFor: Anything beyond study: there is no runnable system
